verdict.rationale: Airwallex's first-party docs describe webhooks as real-time push notifications sent to your application when account events occur. The docs also cover delivery semantics: your endpoint must return 200, each event has a stable id for safe retry handling, and the web app shows delivery status and lets you re-deliver events, so a programmatic consumer can receive them. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of how endpoints are registered and how specific event types are subscribed to, signature verification details, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: Webhooks enable Airwallex to send instant, real-time push notifications to your application when events occur in your Airwallex account.
Your endpoint must respond with a 200 status code so that Airwallex can confirm delivery. Each event has a stable `id` so you can safely handle retries and avoid processing the same event twice.
inspect delivery status (success, queued, or failed) and re-deliver events after downtime or for debugging.
